## f38ce802fe57

**No issue found.** This findings-only audit checked the current version 4.0.0
generator against its canonical flood-fill rule. All 19 retained inputs passed
`generator.self_check` and produced the same output under the generator mirror,
an independent Python flood-fill, and actual Racket execution. Every requested
room-count/color override was observed exactly.

The focused adversarial question was whether partial cuts still allow the old
shortcut that fills between only complete wall rows/columns. It fails on the
accepted 5×7 case at index 0: the seed is in a two-cell room above a partial wall.
Racket changes only `(1,2)` to color 2; the rival additionally colors unreachable
cells `(3,1)` and `(3,2)` (zero-based coordinates). The rival disagreed on
14 of the 19 checked cases. This is evidence against that shortcut,
not a generator defect. Case 1 relocates the seed within the same smallest room
and changes its color to 8; the reference still fills precisely that room.

**Scope and limits.** Inspected only this task's selected generator, summary,
notes/associated decisions, focused tests, and canonical record. There is no
current `evidence/review_index.json` in this task's home. Exercised five canonical
pairs, twelve deterministic generated cases covering easy/medium/hard ×
room_count 3/6 × seed_color 2/8, and the two hand-authored cases. Exact generated
seeds, sample indexes, difficulties, overrides, observed axes, inputs, validator
results, and both Python outputs are retained in `cases.json`. This was not a
full battery or a profile-frequency census. It makes no new claim about inputs
outside the generator's declared framed, single-seed, rectangular-room domain.
